newsitem.title: USA: Gainsco sees Q4 EPS in $0.15-$0.20 range.
newsitem.headline: Gainsco sees Q4 EPS in $0.15-$0.20 range.

text.p: Gainsco Inc chief executive Joseph Macchia said he expects the company to report 1996 fourth quarter earnings of $0.15 to $0.20 a share, well below Wall Street's expectations.
For the full year, he told Reuters he expects earnings of $0.70 to $0.75 a share.
That compares with First Call's fourth quarter consensus estimate of $0.27 a share and full year estimate of $0.85.
Macchia cited fierce competition and a pick-up in business that came too late in the quarter to help 1996's results.
Gross premiums written for 1996 were $110 million, which was at the low end of Gainsco's targeted range.
Gainsco's gross premium goal for 1996 was $115 million, with a range from $110 million to $120 million.
Gross premiums in 1995 were about $108 million.
Macchia said much of the written premiums came in late December, resulting in lower-than-expected earned premiums.
However, he said, he hopes the company will maintain in 1997 the momentum experienced in the last two weeks of 1996.
Macchia said the company's claims experience improved in the fourth quarter, but said it was not enough to make up for the poor experience in the third quarter.
Meanwhile, he said, the company repurchased more than 470,000 shares under its share buyback program.
In addition, the board has authorized the repurchase of an additional 500,000 shares.
The company is scheduled to report 1996 results on February 26.
Macchia also said the company continues to explore the possibility of making an acquisition.
He said the company hired Richard Buxton, formerly with K N Energy Inc as its new merger and acquisition specialist.
Gainsco is scheduled to meet with analysts on Thursday at an insurance industry conference sponsored by the New York Society of Security Analysts.
